newsitem.title: USA: Brady debt mixed in extremely thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt mixed in extremely thin trade.

text.p: Brady bond prices were narrowly mixed at late afternoon but emerging market debt sources said activity remained extremely thin ahead of key U.S. inflation data due out Friday.
"It's very dead. People are waiting for the inflation numbers," said one market analyst, who said there could be a selloff if signs of inflation emerge.
At 1630 EDT/2130 GMT, Brazilian C bonds were unchanged at 75-3/8 bid, while Mexican Pars were 1/4 lower at 70-1/2 bid and Venezuelan DCBs were 7/8 stronger at 86-5/8 bid.
Market experts said a growing consensus that the Federal Reserve will again hike short-term interest rates in May has resulted in many players keeping to the sidelines.

"Volumes aren't that significant. People think the second increase is inevitable, and given that, they want to see how things shake out here. If anything, they are just shortening durations and trimming their portfolios a little bit," said James Barrineau, emerging market strategist at Smith Barney.
Still, market experts said the economic fundamentals of most emerging market countries remain favorable.

They said progress on the privatization front in Brazil, expectations for positive news from Mexico on March inflation data and movement on labor legislation in Venezuela all reflect postive fundamentals.
Among Eastern European credits, Bulgaria IAB bonds were off 7/8 at 57-1/2 bid and Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans were 1/8 better at 77-1/4 .
